header.title: Diversarum hereseon liber: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Philastrius, Saint, Bishop of Brescia
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's stoa0122a.stoa001.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's CSEL (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.

notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0122a.stoa001.opp-l: The second sentence has no main verb until baiulabant (‘carried’); the carving on the stone and the amulets worn on the neck are run together, and the construction is loose.

nodes.text: and for this the Lord commanded Moses to make a bronze serpent and hang it in the midst of the people upon a pole; and those who looked at it were saved from the strikes and from various wounds. To that bronze serpent, then, the people of the Jews sacrificed until King Hezekiah; the Jews also, carving figures on a great stone like an obelisk, which had been set in the temple as a pillar, and on it incisions and impressions made by men’s hands, as if of certain letters, and taking various formulas and placing them on a thin metal plate, carried them on their necks:
